wiki_article:
**AXN as Anti-Suppression Infrastructure: Historical Precedents** is a scholarly paper by Lee Sharks, **with Johannes Sigil composing §§II–III and Rex Fraction on §VI**, with Assembly Chorus consultation preserved in provenance.

It is a **source-engaged supersession** of the developmental version at **#1094**, composed under a standing rule recorded in the decisions register on 18 July 2026: ***engagement with sources is composition-primary*** — reading the literature is part of writing the paper rather than a stage preceding it.

**Section-level attribution to distinct heteronyms** is the Dodecad operating as a division of labour within a single document, the same practice as the Abraham Principle (#1258). The paper argues the AXN identifier system as anti-suppression infrastructure with historical precedents, which places the archive's own identifier work in a lineage rather than presenting it as novel.
